chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was a father of daughters.

key_terms.أبا بنات: Father of daughters — a title of honor emphasizing the Prophet's connection to his daughters, especially Fatima al-Zahra (a.s.)
key_terms.رسول الله: Messenger of God — the most common honorific title for the Prophet Muhammad (saww)

ai.seo_question: Was the Prophet Muhammad a father of daughters?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirmed that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was a father of daughters, situating this as a mark of honor and nobility. This hadith appears in a chapter dedicated to the merits of daughters, countering the pre-Islamic Arabian custom (jahiliyya) that viewed daughters as a source of shame. The early Shia audience would have understood this as a direct theological argument: if the best of creation was honored with daughters, having daughters is not a cause for grief but a divine blessing.
